title: Evaluation of Risk‐Based River Environmental and Recreational Regulations Derived From Waterborne Fecal Indicator Bacteria
content:
Reverse QMRA combined with DALYs at the risk of 10−6 DALY pppy is used to evaluate risk-based river environmental and recreational regulations derived from river fecal coliforms.


ABSTRACT

To protect the health of water recreationists, establishing regulations for exposure duration, annual participation days, and waterborne pathogen levels based on acceptable risk benchmarks is essential. This study employed reverse quantitative microbial risk assessment (QMRA) integrated with disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) to evaluate risk-based river environmental and recreational regulations for the Bitan Scenic Area, Taiwan. Parameter uncertainty and variability were propagated using Monte Carlo simulations. Critical thresholds (5th–95th percentiles) for fecal coliform (FC) concentration, exposure duration, and annual participation days across canoeing, swimming, and fishing were evaluated at an acceptable risk target of 10−6 DALY per person per year and compared with field observations. The results demonstrate that current Taiwanese water-based recreational standards are appropriate, as they fall within the 5th–95th percentile range of the modeled FC critical thresholds. Comparisons with observational data suggest that restrictions on exposure duration are unnecessary because current exposure levels remain within safe limits. However, local authorities should enforce limits on annual participation days for canoeing and fishing to no more than 59 and 63 days/year, respectively.
